business_quality_reasoning: Epic Cleaning has traded since 2022 with a 5.0 Google rating, but only 6 reviews and micro-entity accounts suggest a small operation. The site claims 'over four years' and lists residential, commercial and event cleaning, so there is a real service mix even if scale looks modest.
price_point_reasoning: No prices shown; a typical London domestic or small commercial clean runs £80-£150 per visit.
modernity_gap: A roughly 2020-era WordPress template with gradient buttons, stock photos and a copyright footer stuck at 2020 — it works, but it looks a generation behind current standards.
site_weaknesses: Copyright 2020 footer and dated gradient styling signal an unmaintained site before a visitor reads a word
Stock photography throughout — nothing shows the actual team, vans or real cleans
Single generic testimonial ('Samantha R.') instead of embedded Google reviews, despite a 5.0 rating
No pricing, no booking flow and no service areas — the only action is a contact form at the bottom
Mobile version stacks the desktop layout awkwardly with small tap targets
site_analysis: This is a textbook dated WordPress site: gradient CTAs, stock photos, a 'Why Choose Us' icon grid and one lone testimonial. The structure exists but nothing on the page builds real trust or makes booking easy — no prices, no reviews feed, no named people. It is functional enough not to embarrass, but it will not convince a comparison-shopping London homeowner.
review_summary: Your site has not really been touched since 2020 and it shows — the styling, the stock photos and the single testimonial all make the business look quieter than it is. You have a 5.0 rating that the website barely mentions. Showing your real reviews and making it easy to get a price would turn visits into booked cleans.
outreach_angle: You hold a 5.0 Google rating, but the site still shows a 2020 footer and one generic testimonial — your best proof is invisible to visitors.
